references.text: The psalmist praises God for teaching his hands to fight and his arms to bend the bow of bronze, a parallel to how Joseph's bow remained strong and his arms were made supple by the Mighty One's hands.
Moses' blessing over the tribe of Joseph contains similar themes of fruitfulness and divine strength, reflecting God's support and blessings in Jacob's blessing over Joseph.
Jacob himself refers to God as shepherd (רעה) who has watched over him all his life, which directly mirrors the description of God as 'shepherd, the Rock of Israel' in the blessing over Joseph.
The psalm uses the title 'Mighty One of Jacob' (אביר יעקב), the same divine title used in Gen 49:24 to describe the source of Joseph's strength.
Isaiah uses the title 'Mighty One of Jacob' (אביר יעקב) as Israel's Redeemer, the same title used for God in Jacob's blessing over Joseph.
The psalm addresses God as 'Shepherd of Israel' (רעה ישראל), a direct parallel to the description of God as shepherd and the Rock of Israel in Jacob's blessing.
Hebrews mentions Jacob's faith when he blessed Joseph's sons and Joseph's faith at his deathbed, reflecting trust in the promises given through these blessings.
